R5.statement: at almost every level the fibre of a regular C1 map meets a relatively compact piece in a set of finite H^(n-r) measure
R5.why_needed: the route applies the Eilenberg bound INSIDE a fibre with d = k and a target of dimension m - r, so d + (m - r) = n - r; for the bound to say anything the fibre must carry FINITE H^(n-r) measure, otherwise the right-hand side is infinity and the estimate is vacuous, which is exactly the failure N2 records for the one-step method
R5.how_proved: a COROLLARY of the proved regular coarea formula with weight 1: the total fibre measure integrates to the integral of the coarea Jacobian, finite on a relatively compact piece because the integrand is continuous there, and a finite integral has almost everywhere finite integrand
R5.says_nothing_about: the critical set of v; surjectivity is assumed on all of O
R5.companion_lemma: hausdorffNormalized_ne_top_iff, the finiteness companion of the proved hausdorffNormalized_eq_zero_iff
R5.relative_compactness_is_necessary: EXHIBITED: the first coordinate functional of the plane on S = univ is a submersion everywhere, every other hypothesis holds, but each fibre is a full line of infinite H^1 measure, so the conclusion fails at EVERY level, not merely on a null set of them

R6.statement: a set whose almost every first-coordinate slice across an orthogonal splitting of the target is null is itself null
R6.why_needed: the two slicings produce 'for almost every s, for almost every tau' while the conclusion is about almost every t; R6 joins the two levels
R6.how_proved: assembly of Mathlib's LinearIsometryEquiv.measurePreserving, WithLp.volume_preserving_toLp and Measure.prod_apply
R6.usable_for_the_intended_splitting: the audit instantiates it along Submodule.orthogonalDecomposition and the instances resolve, so the abstract isometry statement is directly usable for the decomposition along the range of the differential
R6.converse_recorded: the audit also proves the converse direction, so R6 is not mistaken for the easy half
